output.summary: KEP-1981 proposed extending the Windows container model to support privileged containers and host network mode for privileged pods, using containerd and CRI, so Windows workloads such as kube-proxy and networking daemons no longer need proxies or host services. The KEP reached status implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Windows lacked privileged container support, so kube-proxy, storage, and networking workloads needed proxies or host-level services, which increased attack surface and complicated updates. The KEP targets privileged access to host resources and host network mode, limited to containerd. Discussion centered on the API shape: reusing the Linux privileged field versus new Windows-specific fields (the thread converged on a HostJob / hostProcess style name).

alternatives.why_not: marosset said reuse would give users false impressions because privileged containers on Windows work very differently than on Linux, and validation could not reliably tell whether a pod targets Windows.

alternatives.option: Use containerd RuntimeClasses and K8s RuntimeClasses
alternatives.why_not: The KEP lists this as an alternative. It was a prototype, and adding the ability to the CRI gives kubelet more control over the security context and checks such as runasnonroot.

alternatives.option: Pass the privileged flag as CRI annotations to containerd
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says adding the field to the CRI spec keeps existing CRI calls working and avoids relying on magic strings.

alternatives.option: Model the feature as a separate isolation mode alongside Hyper-V
alternatives.why_not: random-liu argued it is closer to privileged on Linux (shared host kernel with more privileges) and is better as a pod/container config option than a separate runtime class; the thread did not settle this.

evidence.quote: Support for these scenarios in Windows currently requires workarounds via proxies or other implementations. This proposal aims to extend the Windows container model to support privileged containers.
Adding the field to the CRI spec allows for the existing CRI calls to work as is. The resulting code is cleaner and doesn’t rely on magic strings.
My biggest concern here is that privileged containers on Windows will work very differently than on Linux and re-using the privileged field will give users false impressions about their capabilities.
I spoke with some other folks in MSFT and right now we are considering calling this WindowsOptions.HostJob in the kubernets API and WindowsContainerSecurityContext.HostJobIsolation in the CRI layer
Looks like this enhancement is targeting for stage `stable` for 1.26 (correct me, if otherwise)
